title: Acyclicity of an ordinal inverse limit of complexes
statement: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. For each $\beta<\alpha$, let $K_\beta^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of abelian groups [def-sp-abelian] (graded abelian groups $K_\beta^n$ with homomorphisms $d:K_\beta^n\to K_\beta^{n+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$), and let the complexes form an inverse system indexed by $\alpha$ (for $\gamma<\beta$ there are compatible transition maps $K_\beta^\bullet\to K_\gamma^\bullet$). Assume that every $K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic, meaning $\ker(d:K_\beta^n\to K_\beta^{n+1})=\operatorname{im}(d:K_\beta^{n-1}\to K_\beta^n)$ for every $n$, and, for every $\beta<\alpha$ and every degree $n$, the canonical map $K_\beta^n\to\varprojlim_{\gamma<\beta}K_\gamma^n$ is surjective. Then the inverse-limit complex $\varprojlim_{\beta<\alpha}K_\beta^\bullet$ is acyclic.

proof.text: We argue by transfinite induction on the ordinal alpha, simultaneously for every inverse system satisfying the hypotheses. This strengthened induction hypothesis lets us use, at every proper initial segment beta<alpha, the acyclicity of the earlier inverse limit.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 0AAT (lemma-ML-over-ordinals), proof: transfinite induction paragraph

proof.text: It is enough first to prove exactness at degree 0. Let x=(x_beta) be a degree-0 cocycle in the inverse limit, so each x_beta is a degree-0 cocycle in K_beta. At beta=0, acyclicity of K_0 supplies y_0 in K_0^{-1} with d(y_0)=x_0.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 0AAT (lemma-ML-over-ordinals), proof: degree-zero cocycle and beta=0

proof.text: At a successor beta=gamma+1, choose y'_beta with d(y'_beta)=x_beta using acyclicity of K_beta. The difference y_gamma-f(y'_beta) is a degree-minus-one cocycle in K_gamma, hence equals d(z_gamma) for some z_gamma in K_gamma^{-2}. Surjectivity of K_beta^{-2}\to K_gamma^{-2} lifts z_gamma to z_beta; replacing y'_beta by y_beta=y'_beta+d(z_beta) gives both d(y_beta)=x_beta and f(y_beta)=y_gamma.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 0AAT (lemma-ML-over-ordinals), proof: successor step

proof.text: At a limit beta, let L^bullet=lim_{gamma<beta}K_gamma^bullet and let y_<beta=(y_gamma) be the compatible earlier elements. Its differential is the image of x_beta in L^0. By the induction hypothesis L^bullet is acyclic. Choose u_beta in K_beta^{-1} with d(u_beta)=x_beta using acyclicity of K_beta (x_beta is a degree-0 cocycle of K_beta). The defect y_<beta-f(u_beta) is a degree-minus-one cocycle in L^bullet, so choose w_<beta in L^{-2} with d(w_<beta)=y_<beta-f(u_beta). Surjectivity in degree -2 lifts w_<beta to w_beta in K_beta^{-2}. Then y_beta=u_beta+d(w_beta) satisfies d(y_beta)=x_beta and f(y_beta)=y_<beta, so it is compatible with every earlier y_gamma.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 0AAT (lemma-ML-over-ordinals), proof: limit step

proof.text: The transfinite recursion therefore produces y=(y_beta) in the inverse limit with d(y)=x, proving exactness at degree 0. For any integer n, apply the degree-zero construction to the shifted complexes K_beta[n], whose degree-zero cocycles are precisely degree-n cocycles of K_beta and whose degree-minus-one boundaries are degree-n boundaries of K_beta; the transition maps and the stated degreewise surjectivity are unchanged by shifting. Thus every degree-n cocycle in the inverse-limit complex is a boundary, so the inverse-limit complex is acyclic.
